writeup: TIC 445266372 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 11.61 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry and pixel-level imaging. The primary eclipse produces an 8.84% dimming, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 6.7 sigma significance. The binary signal achieved a detection significance of 106.4 on the Box Least Squares periodogram, with pixel-level confirmation showing a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 42.3 and a centroid offset of 1.6 arcsec from the target. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. However, analysis reveals that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true period is double the initially detected value - a pattern consistent with a real eclipsing system rather than instrumental artifacts. Pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain unaffected by this period correction.
